title: Four direct Node-backed smoke wrappers report success when their only evidence is skipped

observed_behavior: Each wrapper invokes a Node-dependent unittest module directly and treats only a nonzero process exit as failure. Python unittest exits zero when tests are skipped. With Node removed from PATH, all four wrappers returned exit code 0 while reporting skipped tests; the row-detail wrapper skipped both of its discovered tests.
expected_invariant: A canonical smoke wrapper must fail when required execution evidence is absent: at least one intended test must run, and prerequisite-driven skips must be rejected unless the operator explicitly requests a diagnostic allow-skip mode.
root_cause: The four wrappers delegate success semantics to raw unittest exit status and do not parse discovered-test or skipped-test counts. They bypass the repository's shared browser smoke runner, which already treats zero tests and disallowed skips as failures.
failure_scenario: Node is missing or unavailable on a validation host. The wrapper prints OK (skipped=N), exits zero, and can be recorded as passing evidence even though none of the intended JavaScript behavior was exercised.
evidence: With PATH restricted to Windows System32, Test-WebViewCommandEvidenceSmoke.ps1 returned exit 0 with Ran 1 test and OK (skipped=1).

Under the same deterministic condition, Test-WebViewRenameReadinessSmoke.ps1 returned exit 0 with one skip, Test-WebViewRowDetailSmoke.ps1 returned exit 0 with two skips, and Test-WebViewScheduleSmoke.ps1 returned exit 0 with one skip.
The four underlying test modules explicitly raise unittest.SkipTest or call self.skipTest when Node is unavailable.
webview_browser_smoke_common.ps1 lines 188-195 and 262-271 demonstrates the maintained strict alternative by parsing tests/skips and failing missing evidence.
affected_flows: CI or release workflows that call these canonical wrappers
command-evidence, rename-readiness, row-detail, and schedule UI regression evidence
existing_safeguards: The wrappers propagate genuine nonzero Python exits.
The underlying tests clearly label missing Node as skipped rather than fabricating assertions.
The separate shared browser runner rejects skips by default.
safeguard_gap: A successful unittest exit is not equivalent to executed smoke evidence, and these four public wrappers do not consume the skip metadata their tests emit.
tests_present: Underlying Node-backed unittest modules exercise the intended WebView behavior when Node is present.
Shared browser-runner support tests cover strict skip and zero-test behavior for browser wrappers.
tests_missing: Negative wrapper tests proving missing Node produces a nonzero wrapper result for all four direct wrappers.
Machine-readable result checks for discovered, executed, and skipped counts on direct unittest wrappers.
recommended_remediation: Route direct unittest wrappers through a shared bounded runner that captures output, requires a positive executed-test count, rejects skips by default, and emits one structured result. If local diagnosis needs skips, expose an explicit AllowSkippedTests switch and mark the outcome non-passing.
remediation_risk: Low to medium: stricter evidence semantics may expose hosts that were previously green only because Node-backed tests skipped; preserve genuine test exit codes and existing boundary text.
validation_rung: PowerShell parser checks plus deterministic missing-Node negative tests for all four wrappers and normal bundled-runtime executions with zero skips. No representative real-media validation is required.
prior_audit_relationship: Distinct from AUDIT-FIND-W10-003, which is located on two CI workflows and covers their incomplete browser matrix plus raw browser unittest selection. Exact current path-local finding reconciliation found no existing finding on these four direct wrappers.

title: Twelve direct Python smoke wrappers have no aggregate timeout or process-tree cleanup
observed_behavior: All twelve wrappers synchronously invoke Python with PowerShell's call operator and wait without a wrapper-level deadline. None starts a controllable process, kills descendants, emits a timeout outcome, or bounds the final wait. Several invoked tests start temporary API or Node child processes, so a hung test or descendant can pin the wrapper indefinitely.
expected_invariant: Canonical smoke entry points must place a finite aggregate deadline around test execution, terminate the owned process tree on expiry, preserve a distinct timeout exit code, and restore environment/location state even when cleanup is imperfect.
root_cause: The direct wrappers duplicate a minimal invoke-and-check-LASTEXITCODE pattern instead of using a shared bounded process runner. Timeout and descendant-cleanup policy exists only in the browser wrapper family.
failure_scenario: A temporary backend, Node harness, unittest cleanup, or Python test deadlocks. The smoke command never returns, no structured timeout evidence is produced, and callers must rely on an unrelated outer job timeout that may leave descendants behind.
evidence: Exact source inspection found twelve direct Python invocations and zero TimeoutSeconds, WaitForExit(milliseconds), Stop-Process, Kill(true), or process-tree cleanup controls in those wrappers.

The shared browser runner in the same directory starts System.Diagnostics.Process, applies a default 600-second bound, uses Kill(true), and emits timeout metadata, establishing a local lifecycle pattern.
A full direct-wrapper campaign completed 11 wrappers and surfaced one ordinary test failure, proving exit propagation works but exercising no aggregate hang deadline.
affected_flows: operator interruption and deterministic audit evidence
existing_safeguards: The wrappers use try/finally to restore working directory and selected environment variables.
Many individual tests have their own focused timeouts and fixture cleanup, and some outer automation has job-level limits.
safeguard_gap: Per-operation and outer-job safeguards do not bound the public wrapper as a unit, do not classify wrapper timeout, and do not guarantee cleanup of descendants created before a hang.
tests_present: Normal-path executions cover wrapper commands and test-level cleanup.
Browser-runner support tests cover timeout and child-process behavior only for the shared browser runner.
tests_missing: Synthetic hanging-Python and spawned-descendant tests for each direct-runner family.
Assertions for timeout exit code, process-tree termination, environment restoration, and machine-readable timeout evidence.
recommended_remediation: Consolidate the twelve wrappers on a shared direct-test process helper with an explicit default timeout, concurrent bounded output capture, process-tree termination, a bounded post-kill wait, structured outcome data, and exact native exit propagation for non-timeout failures.
remediation_risk: Medium: wrappers cover tests with different legitimate durations and environment needs, so defaults must be configurable without permitting silent unlimited execution.
validation_rung: PowerShell parser checks, synthetic success/nonzero/hang/descendant tests for the shared helper, then the twelve wrapper executions. No representative real-media validation is required because these wrappers use synthetic or temporary fixtures.
prior_audit_relationship: Distinct from AUDIT-FIND-W11-WEB-002, which concerns an inner Python browser timeout leaving a Node-launched browser descendant. Exact current path-local reconciliation found no existing timeout finding on these wrappers.

title: The shared browser runner buffers and replays child output without a byte or line limit
observed_behavior: The runner starts concurrent ReadToEndAsync operations for stdout and stderr, retains both complete strings for as long as the child runs, splits them into another in-memory array, and writes every nonblank line to the host. Its 600-second time bound does not cap emitted bytes or log volume.
expected_invariant: Smoke execution must drain both child streams without deadlock while enforcing explicit per-stream and combined evidence limits, retaining enough head/tail context and reporting exact truncation metadata.
root_cause: Deadlock prevention was implemented with unbounded whole-stream reads and a second full output projection; no byte counter, ring buffer, spool bound, or truncation contract accompanies the timeout.
failure_scenario: A faulty browser/backend test logs continuously during the permitted ten-minute window. The wrapper consumes growing memory, duplicates the data during splitting, and floods CI or terminal logs before the time limit can produce its structured result.
evidence: webview_browser_smoke_common.ps1 lines 158-159 call ReadToEndAsync for both streams; lines 174-187 materialize, split, accumulate, and replay all captured output.
The focused support suite deliberately proves concurrent capture survives roughly 458 KB of chatty stderr, but neither implementation nor tests define a maximum-output outcome.
The structured result records timeout and skip data but contains no captured-byte count, truncation flag, or retained-output policy.
existing_safeguards: Both streams are drained concurrently, preventing the classic stdout/stderr pipe deadlock.
Output parsing and the final structured result occur after process completion.
safeguard_gap: Concurrency bounds waiting time but not memory or output volume; a noisy child can exhaust resources before timeout or prevent the final result from being emitted.
tests_present: test_browser_smoke_support includes a chatty-stderr regression that verifies no pipe deadlock.
Normal and timeout cases assert structured outcomes.
tests_missing: A deliberate over-limit producer with assertions for bounded retained bytes, continued draining, truncation counts, and final structured result.
Separate stdout, stderr, and combined-limit cases.
recommended_remediation: Drain streams incrementally into bounded head/tail or ring buffers while counting total bytes and lines. Continue discarding beyond the retention cap to avoid pipe blockage, emit one truncation notice plus counts in the structured result, and keep summary parsing on a separately bounded channel.
remediation_risk: Medium: output bounding must preserve unittest summary detection and diagnostic tails without reintroducing pipe deadlock or blocking asynchronous readers.
validation_rung: Focused browser-smoke support tests with small configured limits, chatty concurrent streams, timeout, summary-at-tail, and truncation metadata. No real-media validation is required.
prior_audit_relationship: Analogous to AUDIT-FIND-W09-004 on a different process owner, but exact current path-local reconciliation found no prior finding for this shared smoke runner's output retention.

title: A failed timeout kill falls into an unbounded wait while the result claims the process was terminated
observed_behavior: When the timed wait expires, the runner tries Kill(true), catches failure, tries Kill(), suppresses a second failure, and then calls parameterless WaitForExit. If both kill attempts fail or termination does not complete, the timeout branch can block indefinitely. If it eventually proceeds, reason text states that the process was terminated without retaining kill outcome.
expected_invariant: The timeout deadline must remain bounded through termination and stream finalization, and structured evidence must distinguish confirmed tree termination from kill failure or incomplete cleanup.
root_cause: The timeout path has no second bounded termination wait or recorded kill state. Both kill exceptions are discarded before an unconditional infinite WaitForExit.
failure_scenario: Process termination is denied, races with a stuck descendant, or fails at the runtime boundary. A command that already exceeded its declared timeout never returns, and any later result can falsely attest termination rather than reporting cleanup uncertainty.
evidence: webview_browser_smoke_common.ps1 lines 160-168 suppress both Kill exceptions and immediately invokes unbounded WaitForExit().
Lines 176-179 and 235-237 assign timeout exit 124 and say the process was terminated without checking termination success.
Focused timeout tests use a normally killable sleeping child; no case forces Kill failure, delayed termination, or an owned descendant that survives cleanup.
existing_safeguards: PowerShell 7.6 is the documented host, so Kill(true) is available and attempted before the single-process fallback.
A normal killable timeout returns exit 124 and records process_timed_out.
Environment variables and working directory are restored in finally.
safeguard_gap: The primary timeout is not an end-to-end deadline once termination begins, and cleanup failure is neither bounded nor represented.
tests_present: Browser-smoke support tests cover a killable sleeping process and expected timeout result.
tests_missing: Forced Kill(true) and Kill() failure paths.
Bounded post-kill wait, surviving-descendant, stream-finalization, and termination_failed result assertions.
recommended_remediation: Track each termination attempt, use a short bounded post-kill wait, cancel or bound stream finalization, dispose the process in finally, and emit a distinct cleanup_failed or termination_unconfirmed outcome when the tree cannot be proven stopped. Never claim terminated without observed exit.
remediation_risk: Medium: termination behavior varies by Windows process state; preserve exit 124 for confirmed timeouts while giving cleanup failure a distinct nonzero result and actionable evidence.
validation_rung: Synthetic fake-child tests for normal exit, timeout with successful tree kill, primary-kill failure with fallback success, both kills failing, descendant survival, and bounded wall-clock completion. No real-media validation is required.
prior_audit_relationship: Distinct from AUDIT-FIND-W11-WEB-002, which concerns an inner browser harness timeout. This finding is the outer shared PowerShell runner's own unbounded termination-finalization path.
